_comment: Screenshot design spec, read by `ship shots capture|render|verify`. caption-band mode: the finished 1242x2688 composites Apple already serves are the base, and only the caption band is repainted per locale. Geometry is committed rather than re-derived because Figma's render endpoint is quota-limited on the starter plan.

source._frameIdsNote: Only frame 1's node id survived the original extraction. `ship shots figma --export <ids>` needs explicit ids for the rest; the drift check does not, since it reads the file version.
source.note: Cached from the Figma REST node tree. /v1/images 429s after a handful of calls on the starter plan, so the mockup pixels cannot be re-exported on demand — which is why this app repaints Apple's composites instead of rebuilding them.

base._note: Downloaded by `ship shots capture` from the public App Store lookup endpoint — the live English composites, at the spec canvas size.

fonts._note: Cambay covers Latin and Devanagari only, so ja/ko fall back to Noto Sans. Both Noto files are variable: without the explicit wght they open on Regular and every CJK caption renders lighter and narrower than the design.

subtitle._note: The second run the art was authored with. The ramp is measured off the retired ScreenShotAppStore4/5 originals - the only Figma exports still on disk - where the subtitle runs about 0.75x the headline's glyph height with 160px between the two runs' cap tops; the shipping frames' own originals were never kept, so size and gap are tuned against the rendered result rather than read off them. The colour is the art's muted grey; correct it from the originals if they resurface.

type._note: Greedy, not balanced, and inside each frame's own Figma box width — because that is what Figma does. A balanced wrap reads better in isolation but breaks lines where the designer did not: it split frame 2 as 'Log a service / in 15 seconds.' where Figma had 'Log a service in 15 / seconds.'

band._note: The licence for this mode: in all six frames the caption sits on flat background, separated from the mockup — ~94% one solid colour, the remaining 6% being the caption glyphs. flatMin turns that property into a gate, so a redesign that puts artwork in the band fails the render instead of destroying it.

_framesNote: Five frames, in App Store order, measured off the fourth-pass art (August 2026): ScreenShotAppStore3 = vehicle detail with an overdue oil change (red glow), ScreenShotAppStore6 = the garage list, ScreenShotAppStore2 = the log sheet, ScreenShotAppStore1 = full service history, ScreenShotAppStore7 = settings on a purple glow (the privacy frame). ScreenShotAppStore4 (onboarding) and ScreenShotAppStore5 (resale value, a screen the app does not have) are retired and their raws are kept only for the trail. Keys track nothing but identity - the array order is the shipped order, and it is shared with the caption file. mockTop is the first row of the phone mockup; mockH is always canvas.h - mockTop because the mockup runs to the bottom edge. The band above mockTop - 4 is snapped to #000000 in the raw PNGs, keeping only the baked English headline glyphs as the ink the renderer aligns to; the baked grey subtitle is erased, since it cannot survive a band repaint and would skew the ink box the caption block centres on. caption.x/w are symmetric about the canvas centre (621) and sized to the headline's own ink, so a localized string wraps where the art wraps.
_bandShiftNote: The baked headline ink in every raw was moved down (frame 3 +36, 6 +86, 2 +66, 1 +85, 7 +96) so the renderer's block lands where the art actually put it. The renderer centres the headline+subtitle block on the baked ink box, and the box is headline-only because the baked subtitle is erased - so once subtitles started shipping, the block grew upward and every caption rendered 87-148px above the art's own headline. Each delta is the offset between the baked headline's centre and the combined headline+subtitle centre measured off the original art. caption.y follows the moved ink. Nothing below mockTop - 4 was touched.
